sentence: Chalahau is walled, and every arrival goes through a gate and into the gate tally; trouble can only get in where the thorp decides.
fact: compound.inst.hasGates false; only a Palisade ("stakes driven in a rough circle"); no watch to keep a tally; same tab: "Much of Chalahau's perimeter has nobody on it"
inPlace: Chalahau has a wall but no proper gate in it: people come and go by gaps everyone knows, and the wall slows trouble more than it stops it. The thorp has no organized force. Defense here is individual armed citizens, with no command, no training and no way to coordinate a response. The thorp knows it needs specialists against the creatures, and has none of its own to send. The thorp's defense is conventional throughout. What arrives unseen here goes undetected and therefore unanswered.
